pages.text: Among the coconut groves of Konaseema stands an old temple. Its bell had not rung in a hundred years. Nobody knew why.
pages.caption: The temple among the groves

pages.text: To Anusha and Bharat, a sister and brother visiting for the summer holidays, it sounded like a challenge. "Let's find out why the bell does not ring," said Anusha.
pages.caption: Anusha and Bharat

pages.text: In an old trunk at their grandmother's house they found a palm leaf map. Groves, canals, the temple. Near the temple, a small mark: three lines and a circle.
pages.caption: The palm leaf map

pages.text: The two of them walked along the canal bank. Every turn on the map was really there. The wind moved through the coconut palms as if it were telling a secret.
pages.caption: The canal bank

pages.text: Behind the temple was an old well. On the stones of the well, the same mark: three lines and a circle. Bharat said eagerly, "There is something here."
There was no water in the well, only steps. Anusha switched on her torch. At the bottom was a small room, and on its wall, old Telugu letters.
pages.caption: Inside the well

pages.text: They needed their grandmother to read the letters. She came and read slowly. "For the bell to ring, the village must come as one."
Anusha understood. The bell was not broken. One person's strength was not enough to ring it. The bell rope was very heavy and needed ten people pulling together.
That evening every child in the village came to the temple. The elders watched, smiling. They pulled the rope. Once, twice, a third time.
pages.caption: All together

pages.text: The bell rang. The sound rolled over the coconut groves all the way to the canals. Now everyone knew the secret. When we stand together, the bell rings.
pages.caption: The bell rings
